examples.text: Seit ich die Nagelbettentzündung am Zeh habe, kann ich nur noch humpeln.
Die Arme muss wegen ihrem Ischias am Stock humpeln.
Damit Florian aufgrund des verkürzten Beines nicht humpelt, trägt er orthopädische Schuhe, die die Differenz ausgleichen.
Er ist mit dem Gips durch die Gegend gehumpelt.
Sie hat zwei Tage lang stark gehumpelt.
Der Wagen humpelte und rumpelte, als er sich langsam vorwärts bewegte.

glosses: One of the short straps tied between the legs of unfenced horses, allowing them to wander short distances but preventing them from running off.

examples.text: We made it and we hobbled up the stairs. Or I hobbled. My sons didn't hobble, I hobbled.

"Saddle a horse—any horse—only let him be sure and fleet," cried Ashwoode, "and I'll pay you his price thrice over!"
"Well, it's a bargain," replied the groom, promptly; "I don't like to see a gentleman caught in a hobble, if I can help him out of it. […]

glosses: An odd job; a piece of casual work.
To fetter by tying the legs; to restrict (a horse) with hobbles.

examples.text: you hobble your old horse and turn him grazing
The friar was hobbling the same way too.
Pepa runs all over Madrid in high heels and tube skirts that make her hobble and give the impression of restraining a naturally energetic woman.

glosses: To move or proceed roughly or irregularly.

examples.text: The hobbling versification, the mean diction.
